## Functions

### `printf` { #printf }

```c
int printf(const char *format,...);
```

Writes formatted output to the standard output stream (stdout).

| Parameter | Direction | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `format` | in | printf format. |
| `...` | in | Arguments. |

**Returns:** The number of characters printed (excluding the null byte used to end output to strings), or a negative value if an error occurs.

### `vprintf` { #vprintf }

```c
int vprintf(const char *format, va_list args);
```

Writes formatted output to the standard output stream (stdout) using a va_list.

| Parameter | Direction | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `format` | in | printf format. |
| `args` | in | Arguments. |

**Returns:** The number of characters printed (excluding the null byte used to end output to strings), or a negative value if an error occurs.

### `sprintf` { #sprintf }

```c
int sprintf(char *buf, const char *format,...);
```

Writes formatted output to a string.

| Parameter | Direction | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `buf` | out | Output buffer; must be large enough, as nothing limits the length. |
| `format` | in | printf format. |
| `...` | in | Arguments. |

**Returns:** The number of characters written to the buffer (excluding the null byte used to end output to strings), or a negative value if an error occurs.

### `getchar` { #getchar }

```c
int getchar(void);
```

Reads a character from the standard input stream (stdin).

**Returns:** The character read as an unsigned char cast to an int or EOF on end of file or error.

### `scanf` { #scanf }

```c
int scanf(const char *format,...);
```

Reads one line from the console and parses it, like sscanf().

| Parameter | Direction | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `format` | in | scanf format. |
| `...` | out | Where to store the converted items. |

**Returns:** The number of input items successfully matched and assigned, or EOF if an input failure occurs before any items are matched.

### `vscanf` { #vscanf }

**Returns:** The number of input items successfully matched and assigned, or EOF if an input failure occurs before any items are matched.

### `stdio_open_tty` { #stdio_open_tty }

```c
int stdio_open_tty(void);
```

Connects stdio to ttysvc now, rather than on first use.

**Returns:** 0 on success, or -1.

### `stdio_set_raw` { #stdio_set_raw }

```c
int stdio_set_raw(int enable);
```

Switches the console between cooked (line editing and echo by the terminal service, the default) and raw (every byte passed through; the caller echoes).

In raw mode printf still turns "\n" into "\r\n".

The setting survives a reconnect.

| Parameter | Direction | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `enable` | in | Non-zero for raw, 0 for cooked. |

**Returns:** 0 on success, or -1.

### `stdio_close_tty` { #stdio_close_tty }

```c
void stdio_close_tty(void);
```

Detaches from the tty so another program can take the foreground.

The next stdio call attaches again.

### `stdio_route_tty` { #stdio_route_tty }

```c
int stdio_route_tty(const char *name);
```

Routes the standard I/O functions to a specific TTY device.

Reconnects at once, so a bad alias is reported here rather than at the next printf.

| Parameter | Direction | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `name` | in | A ttysvc alias (e.g. "tty0"), or "" for the default endpoint. |

**Returns:** 0 on success, or -1.

### `stdio_use_tty` { #stdio_use_tty }

```c
int stdio_use_tty(uint32_t index);
```

stdio_route_tty() to "tty<index>".

| Parameter | Direction | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `index` | in | Terminal number; only its last decimal digit is used. |

**Returns:** As stdio_route_tty().
